$comment: RAY-CLOUD shared contract 1.0.0-rc.1. Capability id vocabulary. An id never changes meaning; a changed meaning gets a new id. The vocabulary version increments when ids are added.

statusValues.available: provided by the runtime of this release
statusValues.planned: added by this release; not provided until the runtime that ships it lists it in inspect()

managedPostureValues.allowed: may be deployed under the managed posture
managedPostureValues.self-host-only: refused under the managed posture until bounded and certified
managedPostureValues.test-only: staging and conformance only; refused for production under the managed posture

rules: pack derives requires from the spec; authors do not write it. verify re-derives it from the spec in the bundle and refuses a mismatch with RAY_MANIFEST_INVALID reason requires-mismatch.

requires lists only ids with requirableByBundle true, sorted by code point, unique. The schema enforces uniqueness only; a list with an id that is not requirable, or out of order, cannot equal the list derived from the spec and is refused at the derived-fields check (reader step 15) with RAY_MANIFEST_INVALID reason requires-mismatch. The manifest semantics check (reader step 8) does not test it, because an id this runtime does not know must reach the capabilities check (reader step 12) and be refused there as unknown-id.
A runtime refuses a bundle whose requires contains an id that is unknown to its vocabulary (RAY_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED reason unknown-id) or that it does not list in inspect() (reason not-provided).
inspect() lists every id the runtime provides, including runtime-provided ids that bundles cannot require.
Platform identity, sessions, API keys, OIDC and health are part of every runtime and have no capability id.
